newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen, foreign firms sign LNG deal.
newsitem.headline: Yemen, foreign firms sign LNG deal.

text.p: Yemen said on Sunday it signed a deal with foreign companies firming the equity structure of a $5 billion liquefied natural gas (LNG) project expected to start exports by the year 2001.

Oil Minister Mohammad Said al-Attar said under the deal France's Total SA would take a 36 percent stake in the Yemen LNG Company, U.S. Exxon Corp jointly with Hunt Oil would get 30 percent, South Korea's Yukong eight percent and Yemen's government 26 percent.
An Oil Ministry statement issued after the signing said the project's annual capacity would be five million tonnes of LNG "which could be exceeded at a later stage."
It said the project includes building a 320 km pipeline from Marib field to Balhaf on the Arabian Sea as well as setting up production facilities and an export terminal.
"Work on the project is expected to end by the year 2001 and exports will start then," the statement said.

Attar told Reuters after the signing that the project's production capacity could be increased by 300,000 tonnes in the first phase. He said Yemen was talking to Turkey, Japan and South Korea as possible buyers of its LNG.
Construction work tenders will go out in the summer, he said.
In January last year, Exxon, Hunt and Yukong signed a memorandum of participation in the LNG project, which will be operated by Total.
